declarative condition model: 'Only Shake If' OR-gate group + 'Paused When' veto group + plain-language boolean caption ('at least one must be true to shake')

signature_moves: Brand-orange accent override (#F78523) on every active control — selected radio + ON switches — instead of the system accent; systematic, purposeful (carries the wooden-maraca icon warmth into a default-dark settings pane), accessible; the app's whole visual identity inside the UI, and simultaneously a native-tell deviation

Declarative smart-conditions model: when-to-jiggle logic exposed as two plain-language toggle groups with a boolean-clarifying caption (Tesler's Law + recognition-over-recall) rather than a rule editor
defects: Accent not system-bound (native-tell #6) — controls hardcode brand orange rather than controlAccentColor; a blue-accent user still sees orange. Deliberate brand trade-off, but prevents a system-default read
Contrast Dilution (soft) — tertiary group caption ~#7D7D7D on #1B1B1B near ~4:1, under the 4.5:1 body floor
Low UI contrast (soft, native convention) — OFF-switch track ~#373737 vs #222 group ~1.3:1; hairline separators barely present

aesthetic.direction: App UI: template-default native SwiftUI dark settings, differentiated only by a committed warm-orange accent. Brand layer (separate): editorial-playful — high-contrast serif italic display over a bold rounded grotesk, committed sky-blue surface with coral/orange warm accents and an emoji-composite icon.

psychology: Jakob's Law — settings mirror System Settings' grouped-Form conventions, so the pane is learnable at first glance
Von Restorff effect — the lone orange active control pops against the neutral dark field; accent economy makes state instantly readable
Tesler's Law (conservation of complexity) — scheduling complexity absorbed into declarative toggle groups rather than pushed onto the user as scripting
Recognition over recall — the 'at least one must be true to shake' caption spells out the boolean instead of leaving AND/OR ambiguous
Hick's Law (mild violation) — six ungrouped condition switches in one group is a lot to scan, though the OR/veto split contains it
